title: Tiered SLO definitions, burst tolerance and progressive rollback gates for inference runtime
creator: Arielle Park
description: Define a set of tiered SLOs and associated acceptance criteria for hosted, dedicated, and private deployments with explicit burst tolerance windows, per-tenant error budgets, and a deterministic set of progressive rollout gates and automated rollback triggers. This ticket is a product-level PRD to align PM/Eng/Design/SE on targets, monitoring requirements, and rollout guardrails for model and runtime releases.
background: Past releases have shown that single global SLOs do not capture real-world variability: low-tier customers accept higher latency and intermittent throttling while enterprise customers require tighter latency and uptime with formal error budgets. We also observed production bursts that temporarily increase p95 latency but recover within minutes; without defined burst tolerance the platform automatically rolled back releases that were acceptable. This PRD prioritizes predictable behavior during controlled rollouts and avoids over-reactive rollbacks.
problem_statement: Need unambiguous, enforceable SLO definitions and rollout gates that support: (1) per-tier targets, (2) short-duration burst tolerance windows, (3) per-customer error budget accounting for Dedicated/Private variants, and (4) clear automated rollback criteria to reduce false positives during canaries.
goals: Define latency and availability SLOs for three customer tiers (Free/Standard/Enterprise) across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments
Specify burst tolerance windows and how bursts consume error budget
Define per-tenant error budget accounting and admin-visible consumption metrics
Create deterministic progressive rollout gates and safe rollback thresholds for canary/A-B releases
Specify monitoring, dashboards, and alerts required to validate gates during rollouts
non_goals: Detailed implementation of enforcement automations (this will be a follow-up engineering spec)
Changing billing tiers or pricing policies
Defining SLOs for embeddings-only endpoints (handled in separate ticket)
proposed_slos: Free tier (hosted): Latency p95 <= 800ms, p99 <= 1800ms; availability 99.5% monthly
Standard tier (hosted & dedicated): Latency p95 <= 350ms, p99 <= 1200ms; availability 99.9% monthly
Enterprise tier (SLA-backed on Dedicated/Private): Latency p95 <= 200ms, p99 <= 800ms; availability 99.95% monthly
Private on-prem installs: contractual SLOs to be negotiated; default recommended target p95 <= 300ms
error_budgets: Monthly budget = (1 - availability_target) * total_minutes_in_month. Track per-customer for Standard/Enterprise, global for Free tier.
Burst tolerance: allow up to 10 minutes per-incident of p95 breaches without consuming monthly availability budget if latency returns below threshold within 10 minutes.
Sustained degradations beyond burst window consume error budget proportionally; repeated bursts in a rolling 24h window consume error budget cumulative.
Dedicated pools may have reserved emergency buffer (5% of budget) for controlled capacity swings; use requires SE approval and is visible in console
acceptance_criteria: PM, Eng, and SRE agree on numeric SLOs and burst rules for all three tiers documented in this ticket
A mapping table exists showing which endpoints (generation, chat, embeddings) inherit which SLOs
Per-customer error budget calculation formula and display requirements are specified for Console and billing reports
Rollout gate definitions and thresholds are reviewed and signed off by Eng and SRE
A minimal dashboard prototype URL is linked in 'links' that shows p50/p95/p99, availability, and error budget consumption per-customer tier
rollout_gates: Gate 0 (Pre-release checks): unit & integration tests, perf benchmarks within 5% of baseline on canary hardware
Gate 1 (Controlled canary 5% traffic): 30-minute observation window; p95 <= 1.2x tier target AND no increase in per-second error rate > 2x baseline over 10m
Gate 2 (Expanded canary 25% traffic): 2-hour observation window; p95 <= 1.1x tier target AND error budget consumption rate <= planned burn rate
Gate 3 (Ramp to 50%+): 24-hour window with no sustained p99 regressions and daily error budget projection within threshold

Auto-rollback trigger: if during any gate the p95 exceeds 1.5x target for > 15 minutes OR availability drops below threshold for > 10 consecutive minutes, automatically pause rollout and notify on-call
Manual override rules: SE or SRE can temporarily pause auto-rollback with documented mitigation steps; overrides must be logged in the rollout incident trail
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboards: per-tier p50/p95/p99, availability, error budget remaining, active canary traffic percentage
Alerts: SLO burn-rate alert (>3x expected burn for 10m), gate-failure alert (gate-specific), and on-call escalation policy defined
Tracing: request-level sampling to capture latency contributors during canaries; link to trace examples in 'links'
Logs: structured rollout events (start/stop/rollback/override) forwarded to central audit log
dependencies: ENG-4120: per-tenant metrics tagging and persistent customer_id in request pipeline
ENG-4382: Console charting support for per-customer error budget visualization
ENG-4450: Canary traffic routing and rollout automation hooks
SEC-220: Audit log format agreement for rollout events
stakeholders: Engineering: Diego Martinez (owner), Priya Shah (SRE lead)
notes: Next step after sign-off: ENG to produce an implementation spec that includes enforcement hooks and a playbook for manual interventions. Plan a dry-run rollout for a low-traffic model to validate gates before the first runtime release under these rules. Capture learnings in postmortem template.
